ai.short_summary: The European Union and the European Parliament agreed to postpone methane emissions regulations by two years. The delay is attributed to disruptions stemming from the US-Israeli conflict with Iran.
ai.detailed_summary: The European Union and the European Parliament reached an agreement to delay rules requiring oil, gas, and coal importers to report methane emissions by two years. The European Parliament announced on Thursday that the extension is a response to disruptions caused by the US-Israeli war with Iran. This agreed two-year delay surpasses the European Commission's earlier proposal in October for a one-year postponement, which had followed pressure from the United States, France, and other governments. ai.short_summary: The Australian dollar dropped and bonds rallied to three-month highs after October jobs data showed a weaker labour market and sparked rate cut bets.
ai.detailed_summary: The Australian dollar fell on Thursday after a weak jobs report led markets to abandon expectations of further rate hikes and price in rate cuts for next year. The unemployment rate rose to a five-year high of 4.9%, exceeding central bank expectations, following five rate hikes this year that brought the rate to 4.85%. As a result of these economic shifts, swaps no longer price in any risk of a rate increase from the Reserve Bank of Australia, triggering a rally in bonds to three-month highs.

ai.background_ai: The Reserve Bank of Australia is the country's central bank responsible for monetary policy, including setting the cash rate to manage inflation and employment. Economic data releases, such as monthly labour force reports, heavily influence market pricing for future interest rate decisions. The Australian dollar is closely watched by global investors as a barometer of domestic economic health and commodity demand.

events.title: Democrats flip Alaska seat to seal 56-44 US Senate majority

sources.name: SCMP World
sources.title: Democrats flip Alaska seat to seal 56-44 US Senate majority

ai.short_summary: Democrat Mary Peltola won the Alaska US Senate race, defeating Republican Dan Sullivan. The victory gives Democrats a 56-44 Senate majority.
ai.detailed_summary: Democrat Mary Peltola won Alaska's US Senate race on Tuesday, defeating Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan according to US media projections. Peltola secured 50 percent of the first-place votes compared to Sullivan's 46 percent, crossing the 50 percent threshold required to avoid additional rounds under Alaska's ranked-choice voting system. This win marks the Democrats' ninth flip of the midterm elections, extending their Senate majority to 56-44.
ai.significance: The victory secures a commanding 56-44 Senate majority for the Democrats.
ai.background_ai: Alaska uses a ranked-choice voting system for its elections, allowing voters to rank candidates in order of preference. If no candidate receives a majority of first-place votes, lower-ranked candidates are eliminated and their votes redistributed until a winner emerges.
key_facts: Mary Peltola defeated Dan Sullivan in the Alaska US Senate race.
Peltola won 50 percent of first-place votes to Sullivan's 46 percent.
The outcome gives Democrats a 56-44 Senate majority.
This is the ninth flip of the midterm elections for Democrats.
